learning: Iterations 0 to 4 show that pitch (10 to 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), track (0.12 to 0.10 m), gains (kp 1.2 to 1.4) and mass (0.8 to 0.5 kg) have not moved max_error off the 0.06 m floor or removed the one line loss per run. If mass 0.4 kg also fails, the next test is either the lag lever (y = 0.06 m) or the top-speed lever (wheel_radius 0.035, wheel_track 0.10), one at a time.
notes: Mass-only test from the iteration 4 design: 0.5 to 0.4 kg, the minimum allowed. Geometry and controller are otherwise unchanged, so any change in line losses or max_error is attributable to yaw inertia.
rationale: Race evidence from iterations 0 to 4 shows every design ended off_track in all 300 trials. max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track floor, progress is 0.10 to 0.18, and steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.16), so the robot drifts rather than jitters. Iteration 4 (mass 0.5 kg) left one line loss per run and max_error at the floor, and the score moved only from 53.2728 to 53.5316, which is within noise. The Integrator's contingency rule for this case is to try mass 0.4 kg, the allowed minimum, before any other change. I follow that rule. Only mass changes from the iteration 4 geometry (0.5 to 0.4 kg), which keeps the test attributable. The controller is held exactly at the iteration 4 values (base_speed 1.6, kp 1.4, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction), because changing gains would confound the mass result. Geometry matches the Builder's entity0 exactly: 20 mm pitch at x = -0.04 to +0.04, y = 0.04, 16 mm footprints, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.18 x 0.12 m body. Expected: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.06 m. The effect is probably small, because mass has moved little on max_error so far. If line losses persist, the next test is lag (sensor bar at y = 0.06 m) or top speed (wheel_radius 0.035 with wheel_track 0.10), chosen by which evidence appears. Controller_errors and control_effort are requested to catch any integration fault.
